findingDetails.title: Skill-doc checker applies case-sensitive frontmatter matching
findingDetails.evidence: cleanScalar trims and removes quotes but preserves case (lines 72-81), and validateBlock checks raw values against lowercase canonical and alias sets (lines 139-145). The helper lowercases before membership checks (check-frontmatter-values-helper.cjs:59), validate_document.py lowercases at line 1638, and resolveCanonicalContextType lowercases canonical and legacy alias inputs at line 107. Thus mixed-case canonical values can be rejected by the skill-doc checker while accepted by the other lowercasing paths. The inspected helper test also explicitly accepts mixed-case Review and high aliases at lines 40-45.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The four requested readers were inspected at the value lookup and normalization points; the shared list stores lowercase spellings at frontmatter-values.json:7 and :19. The checker test suite was not inspected in this pass.
findingDetails.recommendation: Normalize case consistently before the skill-doc checker performs its canonical and alias membership checks, and add parity coverage for mixed-case canonical and alias values.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: The skill-doc checker may intentionally require lowercase spellings, but no such distinct contract was visible in its inspected value-checking code.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: This could be intentional strictness in the skill-doc checker; the helper test explicitly accepts any case and the other inspected consumers normalize case, so behavior is currently inconsistent.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: A documented case-sensitive contract for the skill-doc checker, paired with tests that establish that distinction, would remove the parity concern.

searchActions.queryOrPath: frontmatter value normalization and membership checks in all four named readers
searchActions.result: The helper and Python validator lowercase before checking all listed aliases; the TypeScript resolver lowercases canonical and legacy alias inputs; the skill-doc checker preserves case before Set membership.

searchLedger.rationale: Case preservation in one consumer conflicts with the case-insensitive behavior of the other inspected consumers and the directly inspected helper test.

searchLedger.hypothesis: A listed document alias may be omitted by one of the frontmatter consumers.

searchActions.result: The three validation paths form accepted sets from canonical entries and alias keys; context-types exports the full document alias map separately from the legacy-only migration alias map.

searchLedger.rationale: Alias keys are drawn from the common data file; the TypeScript module explicitly separates general document aliases from the intentionally narrower legacy migration aliases.
searchLedger.ruledOutReason: The inspected source comments and maps preserve the distinction between frontmatter acceptance and legacy migration.
